title: `Span::enter()` across an await kills tokio workers
description: tracing::Span::enter() returns a thread-local guard. A task that yields while holding one leaves the span entered on that worker, so the next task scheduled there runs inside a span it does not own. The subscriber is eventually asked to clone a span an earlier task already closed, which panics the worker thread; enough dead workers and the runtime has nothing left to poll. The process then presents as a total hang — listeners still accept TCP, nothing answers, background tasks go silent at the same moment — which reads like a lock deadlock and sends you hunting in the wrong place. The give-away is unrelated peers nested inside one another in the log's span field. Fix: attach the span to the future with tracing::Instrument instead of entering it. clippy::await_holding_lock does not catch this, since a span guard is not a lock.
whenToUse: Any async code that wants a span: server accept loops, per-request spans, background tasks.
whenNotToUse: Synchronous code, where the guard's scope and the thread's work genuinely coincide — there `enter()` is correct.
